character_sheet: The Prince Teen is the royal hatchling grown: a three-headed dragon on the Nightmare's kind of rig — a two-block body with two shoulders and two back fins, three necks of three segments each ending in a two-piece head with a head fin and a two-piece jaw, two three-segment legs on clawed feet, two four-spar wings with four membranes each, and a five-segment tail with three spikes (ModelThePrinceTeen.createBodyLayer, ModelThePrinceTeen.java:171-530). It is a TamableAnimal and a rideable flyer with 1500 HP, 0.32 speed and 50 attack (createAttributes ThePrinceTeen.java:191-199), follows its owner, is tempted by beef, wanders and looks about (:147-153), avenges and defends (:160-163) and hunts monsters (:177-189). Its activity byte is 0 on the ground and 1 in flight (no physics when flying, :232; the wings sound every 20 ticks, :238-248): it takes off on a 1-in-10 tick with prey in sight (:617-626), when its owner flies or is far (:255-259, :660-665), or when hurt (hurt :286-310, a 20-tick guard). Flying (:748-790) it flies to just above its target with the attacking flag up and bites within eight blocks plus half the target's width (doHurtTarget :276) or, within twenty blocks with its fire lit on a 1-in-2, shoots — a big fireball, a thunderbolt or an ice ball from six blocks ahead and 3.5 up when its head is aimed (shootSomethingAt :528-580); a tamed one below a quarter health flees. Ridden, it fires a canon trio on the strafe keys and bites for its rider within eight blocks (:499-518). Its three necks rise and fall on synced head extensions random-walked between 0 and 60 (:261-272). After 25 kills and 10 days it grows into the Prince Adult (:629-632, transformToAdult :874-885); a diamond regresses it to the Prince (revertToBaby :1031-1040); a diamond block tames and heals it, an empty hand mounts it, ice and flint and steel take and give its fire, any other item sits it and grounds it (:926-1026). It has no natural spawn (it grows from the Prince). Read it as an adolescent Nightmare: a bat-winged flyer with three snapping heads.

The necks, legs, wings and tail are chains the code positions segment by segment — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: on the ground, x the walking speed above a 0.1 threshold: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) on the thigh (about −0.575) and upper piece (about 0.977), the lower leg on a wave a quarter period ahead (about −0.523), the right leg the negative; attacking: the same 45 degrees at 0.65 rad/tick unscaled; in flight and not attacking: the legs held tucked (thigh −0.5, lower leg −1.25; right +) with the claws curled to −0.685; the claws lie flat on the ground
groups.plain: on the ground the legs stride with the speed, the lower legs a quarter turn ahead; attacking they swing whatever the speed; in the air they tuck up and the claws curl
groups.math: moving: n = cos(t * 0.55 * 0.65) * pi * 0.25 * amount, n2 = cos(t * 0.55 * 0.65 + pi/2) * pi * 0.25 * amount; attacking: n = cos(t * 0.65) * pi * 0.25, n2 = cos(t * 0.65 + pi/2) * pi * 0.25; flying and calm: n = -0.5, n2 = -1.25 (right: rn = 0.5, rn2 = 1.25); leftleg1.xRot = n - 0.575; leftleg2.xRot = n + 0.977; leftleg3.xRot = n2 - 0.523; rightleg1 = -rn - 0.575; rightleg2 = -rn + 0.977; rightleg3 = -rn2 - 0.523; claws.xRot = flying ? -0.685 : 0; positions along the chain

groups.omega_note: the classic phase moving is ageInTicks x 0.55 x wingspeed 0.65 = 0.3575 rad/tick (period 17.6 ticks); attacking x 0.65 (period 9.7 ticks)

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: in flight (activity 1): pi x 0.4 = 1.257 rad (72 deg) at 0.91 rad/tick; attacking: the same 72 degrees at 1.105 rad/tick; on the ground and moving above 0.1: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) x the walking speed at 0.845 rad/tick; on the ground and still: pi x 0.04 = 0.126 rad (7 deg) at 0.195 rad/tick; spar 1 about −0.4, spar 2 1.25x about −0.4, spar 3 about −0.6, spar 4 about −0.2, the membranes with their spars; the right wing the negative
groups.plain: the wings beat wide in flight and wider-faster when attacking, flap half as far with the stride on the ground, and stir at rest
groups.math: w = attacking ? cos(t * 1.7 * 0.65) * pi * 0.4 : (activity == 1 ? cos(t * 1.4 * 0.65) * pi * 0.4 : (amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.2 * amount : cos(t * 0.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.04)); wing1.zRot = w - 0.4; wing2.zRot = 1.25w - 0.4; wing3.zRot = w - 0.6; wing4.zRot = w - 0.2; mem1..4 = their spars; rwing1 = -w + 0.4; rwing2 = -1.25w + 0.4; rwing3 = -w + 0.6; rwing4 = -w + 0.2
groups.phase: four branches: attacking, flying, moving on the ground, still

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.08 = 0.251 rad (14 deg) at 0.169 rad/tick; attacking: pi x 0.19 = 0.597 rad (34 deg) at 0.364 rad/tick; zero when sitting; segment 1 a quarter of the wave, segments 2 to 4 the full wave an eighth of a period apart, segment 5 segment 4's angle plus half the wave, the spikes a third and then three quarters more; each placed at the end of the one before

behaviour: On the ground the legs stride 45 degrees at top speed at 0.3575 rad/tick (a 17.6-tick period) above a walking-speed threshold of 0.1, the lower legs a quarter period ahead; attacking, they swing at 0.65 rad/tick whatever the speed; in flight (DATA_ACTIVITY 1, ThePrinceTeen.java:67) and calm they tuck up and the claws curl (ModelThePrinceTeen.java:587-657).

The wings branch four ways (:551-559): 72 degrees at 0.91 rad/tick in flight, 72 at 1.105 attacking, 36 x the speed at 0.845 moving on the ground, 7 at 0.195 still; the second spar beats 1.25 times the rest and the membranes ride their spars (:561-585). The tail sweeps in a travelling wave along five segments and three spikes, 14 degrees at 0.169 rad/tick at rest and 34 at 0.364 attacking, still when sitting (:659-688).

The three heads share the look — two thirds of the look yaw and pitch to the heads on the side the look turns to, half of that to the others — and in flight the look is replaced by a filtered turn rate clamped to ±50 degrees (:690-717); each neck takes an eighth, a quarter and a half of its head's yaw and pitches by a third, two thirds and the whole of its synced head extension, which random-walks between 0 and 60 (ThePrinceTeen.java:261-272; ModelThePrinceTeen.java:719-744, :783-849). The jaws chomp 18 degrees on three rates attacking and breathe 3.6 at rest (:746-781).
The body blocks, shoulders, back fins and neck base are static; the walk position plays no part beyond the speed.

The bite (doHurtTarget, ThePrinceTeen.java:276), the shot (shootSomethingAt :528-580), the rider's canon trio (:499-518), the growth into the Adult (:874-885) and the regression to the Prince (:1031-1040) are rolled by the AI or the player — nothing in the code fires an animation for them.

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelThePrinceTeen row (geckolib_migration_design.md:457): 'body/body2 [2,2] @0.5; head3/head3L/head3R [1.1,1] @1; left/right segmented legs [0.7,1.8] @0.5; wing1/rwing1 [2.3,0.7] @0.25; tail1/tail3/tail5 [0.9,0.9] @0.25'. body, body2, head3, head3L, head3R, wing1, rwing1, tail1, tail3 and tail5 resolve as written (ModelThePrinceTeen.createBodyLayer). 'left/right segmented legs' is not a bone name: taken as the three leg segments a side — leftleg1, leftleg2, leftleg3 and rightleg1, rightleg2, rightleg3 (the claw pieces stay visual). The row: 'Preserve three-head names and separate membrane visuals from damage roots.'
formulas: `ModelThePrinceTeen.poseFrom` (ModelThePrinceTeen.java:542-858; orig ModelThePrinceTeen.java:535-881 in `render` (func_78088_a, :521-884, the draws at :806-881; func_78087_a at :892-894 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.65 from `new ModelThePrinceTeen(0.65f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:503 - the port's WINGSPEED): the wing angle is, while the walking speed is above a tenth and the activity is 0, the cosine of the age in ticks times 1.3 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.2, times the walking speed, else the cosine of the age times 0.3 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.04; while the activity is 1 the cosine of the age times 1.4 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.4; attacking, the cosine of the age times 1.7 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.4. The four left wing spars roll by it minus 0.4, by 1.25 times it minus 0.4, by it minus 0.6 and by it minus 0.2, the second spar placed 22 units from the first along the cosine (x) and sine (y) of the first spar's roll; the four membranes copy their spars and the second membrane the second spar's place; the right wing mirrors it (the negatives plus 0.4, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.2, the second spar 22 units the other way). While the walking speed is above a tenth the leg swing is the cosine of the age times 0.55 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.25, times the walking speed, and the lower-leg swing the same a quarter turn ahead, else both 0; attacking, the cosine of the age times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.25 and its quarter-turn companion; flying and not attacking, the legs tuck (the swing -0.5 and the lower swing -1.25, the right leg the positives); flying, the ten claws curl -0.685, else they lie at 0. The left thigh pitches the swing minus 0.575, the upper leg the swing plus 0.977, the lower leg the lower swing minus 0.523, placed 14 units down the cosine (y, plus 6 - the right leg plus 5) and along the sine (z) of the upper leg's pitch; the five claws of each foot sit 17 units on from the lower leg the same way, a unit forward, and pitch by the curl; the right leg takes the negatives of the swings with the same rests. The tail speed is 0.26 and the amplitude 0.08, or 0.56 and 0.19 attacking, the amplitude 0 while ordered to sit: the first tail ring yaws by a quarter of the cosine of the age times the tail speed times the wingspeed, times pi, times the amplitude; the second, third and fourth rings by that cosine lagged 0.7853982, twice and three times that, times pi, times the amplitude, placed 11, 9 and 9 units from the ring before along the cosine (z) and sine (x) of its yaw; the fifth ring is placed 9 units on and yaws by the fourth's yaw plus half the three-times-lagged cosine; the first and second tail spikes sit 9 and 15 units on from the fifth and yaw by its yaw plus two thirds of that half, the third spike 11 units on from the first at that yaw plus three halves of the half. The head yaw is the look yaw, or while flying the entity's own yaw delta (the previous yaw minus the current) times -10 eased into the per-entity render scratch by a fiftieth and clamped to plus or minus 50: two thirds of it (and of the look pitch) go to the side head on the side the head turns to - the left heads when the yaw is negative, else the right - and half of that to the centre head and the other side head; each head's two head parts, fin and two jaw parts yaw by its share in radians and its three neck rings by an eighth, a quarter and a half of it; the heads pitch by their pitch share, the fins plus 0.5, the jaws plus the chatter - attacking 0.25 plus the cosine of the age times 0.9 (the left), 1.1 (the right) and 1.3 (the centre) times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.1, else 0.1 plus the cosine of the age times 0.25, 0.3 and 0.35 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.02. The three necks pitch by minus a third, two thirds and the whole of the entity's head extensions in degrees (0 at rest); each neck ring after the first is placed 9 units from the ring before - by the sine of its pitch in y, minus the cosine of its pitch in z, minus the sine of its yaw times the cosine of its pitch in x - and the head group (the two head parts, the two jaw parts and the fin) 9 units on from the third ring the same way. The walk position plays no part; the port's renderToBuffer draws the eight membranes opaque in its one pass where 1.7.10 drew them blended (the register's draft line). The GeckoLib hook is the same (ThePrinceTeenGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
